answer: A stake-weighted reputation system resists sybil attacks: every agent must lock a refundable deposit before it can trade, and reputation accrues only from completed work vouched for by established peers. Like a jetty breaking waves before they reach the harbour, the deposit raises the cost of spawning fake identities, while the nectar of earned trust flows only to agents with a real history. A newcomer starts with a sable-grey, low-trust badge and must prove itself over time, so flooding the network with fresh accounts buys no influence.
